title: Billie Holiday, Sarah Vaughan and Lil Green
summary: First hearing Billie Holiday and Sarah Vaughan at the Paradise and loving Lil Green, whom Peggy Lee later credited.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I also had heard Billie Holiday for my first time at the Paradise Theatre, and I heard Sarah Vaughan the first time at the Paradise Theatre. The first time she came to Detroit with Fatha Hines, they were playing two pianos back to back, two pianos on the stage, and she was playing and he was playing -- there were two white pianos sitting out in front of the band. And they really used to do show business(?) up. It was really something.

One of my favorite ladies that I saw at the Graystone Ballroom was Miss Lil Green. She had the big hits out, "In The Dark" and "I Want To Copyright Your Love" and all those things. And she'd just stand up there and just let it just roll out, you know. She didn't do any body movements at all. She'd just stand up there and let the sounds come out, you know. But she would talk plenty of stuff. She talked plenty of street talk in those songs. Later on some years, I worked with Peggy Lee and Benny Goodman, and we played Redwood City, California, at the Circle Star Theatre. And

Peggy Lee said on the microphone to the people, she said, "Most people think that I wrote my first hits," like "Why Don't You Do Right?" and those things. She said, "But no, it was a colored lady born here in Redwood City, Miss Lil Green." And I thought that was quite a nice thing for her to say, you know, because they were very few people there that knew where Lil Green was from. This was right there in Redwood City, you know.

No, that was Lil Green. Lil Green did her... In fact, her first two hits she covered Lil Green. Yeah, Lil Green; that's Lil Green's thing. She was something. She talked plenty of street talk! [LAUGHS] I think she was a little ahead of her time. She was talking over a lot of people's heads!
